title: Birch-minus-beech autumn interval trends were uncertain in four Swiss samples in 1996-2023
abstract: We tested change in the gap from 50 percent leaf colour to 50 percent leaf fall for birch relative to beech. We used 1,566 paired station-years at 66 Swiss stations in two regions and two periods, 1996-2009 and 2010-2023. Station-adjusted slopes ranged from -1.19 to +1.26 days per decade. All four intervals with a correction for four tests included zero. No-weight fits, stricter record rules and removal of negative gaps also left the slopes uncertain. Exact linear bounds show that errors of up to one day in each of four dates permit both signs in every sample. These are worst-case bounds, not measured errors. Shared station-year date shifts cancel, but differential reporting errors need not cancel. Short periods, missing visits, selected stations and a common network limit the result. No weather or pollution attribution was tested. The package includes code, source hashes, aggregate results, checks and a figure.

display.caption: Trend uncertainty and possible date errors for the birch-minus-beech interval. Source: MeteoSwiss. Date-error bounds are not confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Prior colour-to-fall weather analysis uses overlapping beech observations. We test paired birch-minus-beech time trends and date-error bounds.
